name: Bun bo Hue
summary: Rice noodles in a beef-and-pork broth, with lemongrass and shrimp paste. Vietnam Tourism records the bowl as heartier than pho, and also as hotter than pho.
origin: Hue. The culture department places the bowl at Dong Ba market.
culture: Vietnam Tourism treats bun bo Hue as the heartier bowl beside pho. The city’s culture department ties the bowl it describes to Dong Ba market: beef and pork bones, beef, pork loaf, hock, banana flower, and herbs.
texture: The national page puts beef brisket in the bowl with pork hock, trotter, congealed blood, and loin, over rice noodles. The culture department also names banana flower.
taste: Vietnam Tourism seasons the broth with garlic, shallots, shrimp paste, lemongrass, herbs, and lime. One account names chili and calls the bowl hotter than pho. Vietnam Tourism is also recorded as paprika, and as heartier than pho rather than hotter. The city’s culture department calls the broth rich from the beef and pork bones.
howToEat: Herbs and lime come with the bowl.
Eat it at Dong Ba. A house number and a clock hour are Check on arrival.
where: Dong Ba market. The street number is Check on arrival.
In Da Nang, Bà Hương at 229 Đống Đa serves it. The Hue bowl is the one to judge.

In Ho Chi Minh City, spicy beef rice vermicelli followed Hue people here. The bowl is fuller than in Hue: more meat and rolls, a rich spicy broth, beef with pork sausage, and fresh vegetables. The broth has a sweet taste of sugar, which softens the strong smell of shrimp paste. Anthony Bourdain once recognized the Hue bowl as one of the most delicious dishes in the world.
seoDescription: A beef-and-pork noodle bowl, recorded as heartier than pho and also as hotter, eaten at Dong Ba in Hue. The price and the hour are Check on arrival.
